flightPaths.departs: Jets to the north and west fly straight ahead 'for several miles', then turn right, then a shallow second right (19R WACKO to NW; 19R BIXAD wraps right round to the NE then north), splitting north of Brookfield above ~5000 ft. Non-jets use a radar SID via Maroochydore. Not used 10pm-6am (night noise rule). A 15 degree angled-off-centreline change for the straight section was only floated as a possible option in the 2022 review, not confirmed.
flightPaths.arrives: This is the end used for SODPROPS arrivals and 19 operations: arrivals come in over Moreton Bay. ILS arrivals join final about 10-12 NM (about 18-22 km) out; visual joins about 4 NM (7.5 km) out; RNP-AR curved arrivals exist. Since 9 Jul 2026 Package 3 moved northern arrivals to this end further north over water (around 59,000 fewer people overflown).

flightPaths.departs: Southbound/eastbound jets (GUMKI, SANEG, SCOTT) turn LEFT soon after takeoff and head south first (turn after 600 ft and 3 DME per the EIS), then east or north-east; non-jets on a radar SID turn tight left to heading 110 along the coast. At night (10pm-6am, when SODPROPS is not available) northbound jets use 19L WACKO/BIXAD: straight ahead for several miles then turn right, parallel to the 19R routes.
flightPaths.arrives: 19 operations: arrivals over Moreton Bay onto 19L; ILS final about 10-12 NM, straight. 19L is the high-side parallel approach (joins at 3,000 ft).

flightPaths.departs: Over Moreton Bay: jets use the 01L WACKO SID, initially about 2 km west of the old 01 path and converging with northbound paths over the Bay. Non-jets (about 30% of traffic) follow a radar heading of 340 degrees (magnetic; runway heading is 010, so about 30 degrees left) over Redcliffe. Night use of this runway over land is restricted; a safety study for night over-airport departures is underway.
flightPaths.arrives: 01 operations: arrivals come in over the city. ILS final starts about 12 NM (about 22 km) out; visual final about 4 NM (7.5 km); RNP-AR curved arrivals exist; Chevron airspace is radar vectored. Package 3 redesigned the southern arrivals for independent parallel ops (about 35,000 fewer people overflown); regular independent parallel use not expected until late 2027.

flightPaths.departs: Over Moreton Bay. Jets to southern and eastern destinations turn RIGHT at the Brisbane VOR (about 1 NM north of the upwind threshold, i.e. very soon after take-off) and head south-east over the bay; Package 3 (from 9 Jul 2026) shifts these south-east departures further east (about 44,500 fewer people overflown). Under SODPROPS this is the only jet departure runway and jets go north over the bay. Radar-SID non-jets also use bay routes.
flightPaths.arrives: 01 operations: arrivals over the city/south (Archerfield area and then up the coast), straight ILS final from about 12 NM, curved RNP-AR also in use. 01R is the low-side approach.

flightPaths.departs: Rules that change usage: no curfew, but night noise rules. Day (6am-10pm) preferred: 19L/19R both arriving and departing (arrivals over Moreton Bay, departures over the city), then 01L/01R. Night (10pm-6am) preferred order: SODPROPS (arrive 19R, depart 01R, all over the bay), reciprocal ops (arrive 19L/R, depart 01R), legacy runway departures 19L over land, legacy arrivals 01R. New runway over land at night only for emergencies/severe weather. SODPROPS needs downwind max 5 kt, crosswind max 20 kt, dry runway, cloud above 2,500 ft, visibility 8 km or more (2007 EIS criteria; the airport page names visibility, cloud, wind and runway surface). An 18-month tailwind trial lets pilots request over-water runways 10pm-6am.
flightPaths.arrives: The map's 26 km straight-in is longer than the published ILS final (about 10-12 NM = 18-22 km); visual finals are about 7.5 km and RNP-AR arrivals are curved. Suggest arrKm about 22 for YBBN. Note the map draws every departure from every runway end, whereas in reality each runway is used in only some modes.

other.correct: Brisbane Skytower, 222 Margaret Street, 274.3 m (900 ft), 90 floors, completed 2019, tallest in Brisbane. The research file says 'about 270 m'; the region file only shows the name, so nothing is wrong on the map itself.

regions/qld.js has future:null, but qld_infra.json defines a future scenario 'After independent parallel runway operations start (late 2027)'. As written, the map shows no future toggle for Brisbane. Both existing parallel runways are already open, so there is no new runway to draw; the scenario would only be explanatory text. The late-2027 date is supported by Airservices: Package 3 changes began 9 July 2026, regular independent parallel runway operations (IPRO) not expected until late 2027. Decide whether to keep null on purpose.

No curfew (PIR/airport text); night rules instead: 10pm-6am preferred order is SODPROPS, then reciprocal ops, then legacy-runway departures, then legacy arrivals; new runway over land only for emergencies or severe weather. Our note says SODPROPS is used 'at night when wind and traffic allow', which is right. SODPROPS also needs visibility, cloud, wind and dry runway (EIS 2007 limits: downwind max 5 kt, crosswind max 20 kt, cloud above 2,500 ft, visibility 8 km). Not checked: the claim '3.8% of movements in early 2025 against a 5.3% target'.

Airservices confirms: northern arrivals to the new runway moved further north over water (about 59,000 fewer overflown, incl. southern Bribie Island); southern arrivals redesigned for independent parallel ops (about 35,000 fewer), starting 9 July 2026; legacy-runway south-east departures shifted further east (about 44,500 fewer). Not checked: the Bulimba, Russell Island and CASA-approval details.
